items.feedback: Right. What makes it an agent is the loop: the model picks an action, the program runs it, the result comes back, and it repeats. A longer prompt or a bigger model still gives you one call.

Not quite. You picked a, 'it read the calendar by opening the booking system on its own', but the model only writes text. What it outputs is a request like check_calendar(machine="laser cutter", date="tomorrow"), which is option c. Your program runs the function and sends the entries back, so the model never touches the booking system.
Right. The agent is stuck repeating the same failing step, so more room or more steps won't help. A step limit ends the loop and reports back, so a person can take over.

Not quite. You said 1, with 'it runs the 3 tools itself', but your program runs the tools, not the model. Each model call ends with one tool request or the final answer: 3 tool requests + 1 final answer = 4 calls.

Partly right. 'It sends it back to the model' is correct, but you left out why: the model needs the result in its next input to pick its next step or write the final answer. For example, once check_calendar returns 'free at 3 pm', the model needs that text to decide to check the training record next.

Partly right. The first part is correct: the model gets each tool's name and a short description, and picks the one that fits. The wrong part is 'it also remembers on its own which tool it picked in earlier sessions'. A model only sees the text it is sent this time: if it picked check_calendar last week, it starts blank today unless your program pastes 'last time: check_calendar' into the text it sends.

summary: You've got the agent loop, why a stuck loop needs a step limit, and that the model chooses tools from their descriptions. The thing to fix is who does what: the model only writes a request, and your program runs the tool and feeds the result back. Reread learning record 0002, then redo q4 in your own words, saying which steps are model calls and which are your program.
